skill.name: design-to-production
skill.description: Converts HTML prototypes into scaffolded React and TypeScript components with guided shadcn/ui mapping, glassmorphism classes, and lightweight quality validation.
skill.summary: Analyze HTML prototypes, scaffold React components, and validate local frontend conventions.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: All 121 static matches are false positives from documentation syntax, expected hidden install paths, quoted shell substitutions, or fixed directory anchors. Semantic review found an arbitrary file-creation risk in the scaffolder and unrestricted local input paths in two scripts. No prompt injection, network activity, credential access, or exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Scaffold arguments can escape the intended output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist component, module, and template names. Resolve the output path and reject any path outside the selected module components directory.

remediation.issue: Prototype and component paths can reference files outside expected project directories.
remediation.suggestion: Canonicalize each input path and require containment within approved prototype or frontend source roots before reading the file.

remediation.issue: Scaffold values are interpolated directly into sed replacement expressions.
remediation.suggestion: Validate identifiers before use and escape sed replacement characters, or replace placeholders with a structured template renderer.

static_findings.snippet: These are NOT valid DevPrep AI glassmorphism classes:
| `interactive-card` | Buttons, forms, user actions | Card, Button, Input, event handlers |
| `display-card` | Read-only content, stats | Card, Typography, badges |
| `layout-section` | Page sections, containers | Layout wrapper, grid/flex patterns |

Detected: Complex layout, grid pattern → layout-section template

content.user_title: Convert HTML Prototypes into React Components
content.value_statement: Hand-converting prototypes creates repetitive mapping and setup work. This skill analyzes HTML, guides component choices, scaffolds React files, and checks local conventions.
actual_capabilities: Extracts component names, glassmorphism classes, interactive elements, and basic layout patterns from local HTML prototypes.
Guides shadcn/ui component mapping and module placement decisions.
Scaffolds React TypeScript components from three bundled templates.
Checks file length, interface prefixes, any usage, class names, and relative import counts.
Provides references for glassmorphism classes, shadcn/ui choices, and recurring layouts.
limitations: Assumes the DevPrep AI frontend structure, module paths, aliases, and glassmorphism conventions.
The target module must already exist, and developers must implement business logic manually.
The props argument is documented but is not applied by the scaffolding script.
Validation uses text matching and does not run TypeScript, tests, accessibility checks, visual checks, or complexity analysis.

use_cases.title: Implement a Prototype
use_cases.description: Turn an approved HTML prototype into a typed component scaffold with mapped controls and styling classes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Design Components
use_cases.description: Map repeated prototype patterns to shared shadcn/ui components and approved glassmorphism utilities.

use_cases.title: Review Component Conventions
use_cases.description: Check generated or edited components for selected size, typing, styling, and import conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Prototype
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [HTML path]. Summarize its component name, interactive elements, layout pattern, and glassmorphism classes. Do not create files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Map Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Map [HTML path] to shadcn/ui components and approved glassmorphism classes. Ask me to confirm the component name and target module.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Scaffold [ComponentName] in [module] with the [template] template. Show the target path and ask before overwriting any existing file.

prompt_templates.title: Implement and Validate
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [HTML path] into a production React component for [module]. Preserve behavior, implement typed props, validate it, and report remaining manual work.

output_examples.input: Analyze the hints panel prototype without creating files.
output_examples.output: A structure summary identifies the proposed component name, buttons, layout, styling classes, and a suitable interactive-card template.

output_examples.input: Scaffold HintsPanel in the practice module.
output_examples.output: A typed component file is generated from the selected template, with shared imports, styling classes, and TODO markers for application logic.

output: Reports the file length and interface naming result.
Flags any usage, unsupported glassmorphism classes, and excessive relative imports.
Returns a pass, warning, or failure summary.

best_practices: Review the extracted structure and confirm the component name, module, and shared controls before scaffolding.
Use simple allowlisted identifiers and verify every generated output path before approving file creation.
Run TypeScript, tests, accessibility checks, and visual review after the bundled validator.
anti_patterns: Do not pass absolute paths or traversal segments to any bundled script.
Do not treat generated TODOs as completed business logic.
Do not rely on text-based validation as proof of production readiness.

faq.question: Which prototypes does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets local HTML prototypes using the DevPrep AI glassmorphism and frontend conventions.

faq.question: Does it fully convert HTML behavior?
faq.answer: No. It extracts structure and scaffolds a component, while developers implement state, handlers, data access, and business rules.

faq.question: Which React templates are included?
faq.answer: It includes interactive-card, display-card, and layout-section templates.

faq.question: Does validation run the TypeScript compiler or tests?
faq.answer: No. The validator uses shell text checks for selected conventions.

faq.question: Can it create a missing module?
faq.answer: No. The target module must already exist before component scaffolding.

faq.question: Is it safe to use untrusted path values?
faq.answer: No. Use project-relative paths and review resolved inputs and outputs until the scripts add containment checks.
